HRA Analysis: SQUAMISH (5) sat without cover two starts ago when finishing third behind Northern Heights and Darcys Fireball. He looks to be dropping back in class into this race and is a horse which could be put into the race if the tempo permitted. He should be hard to beat. DAIMYO (4) has good early speed and can look to press forward and find a prominent position in this race. He was able to secure a good run behind the leader recently at this track and sprinted best to score late. LEAF STRIDE (6) joins the stable of Shawn Grimsey having previously done his racing in NSW at a good level. He ran a good fourth last time out in the trotters cup behind Ghandi Mail. LAYDOWNLUNA (3) has good early speed and may be able to work across early before having options from there. If she can secure the right run she can be running on late in this race. SELECTIONS: SQUAMISH (5), DAIMYO (4), LEAF STRIDE (6), LAYDOWNLUNA (3) SUGGESTED BET: SQUAMISH (5) to win.

FIRE AND PASSION (6) looks a clear standout on class in this race and appears very hard top beat despite drawing outside the front row. He trialled up nicely recently at this track when beating Shes Crunchy who raced without a lot of luck on Saturday when returning. UNCLE TONY (1) was able to lead and win two starts ago over the 1660 at Albion Park beating Tilly Jayne. He has always been a horse best served when driven with a sit and can look to lead and sit on the likely short priced favourite in this race FIRE AND PASSION (6). WILLIAMS (2) with no back line in this race he should be able to drop in and secure the right type of run in this race. He took on a strong race last time out taken out by Mostert and battled away fairly there for third. BITE THE EAR MIKE (3) secured an ideal run on the back of his stablemate Barracuda last time out at Marburg and didn’t finish the race off there finishing fifth albeit it not beaten far. He may just be better suited around the bigger track and should secure a good run on the pegs. SELECTIONS: FIRE AND PASSION (6), UNCLE TONY (1), WILLIAMS (2), BITE THE EAR MIKE (3) SUGGESTED BET: UNCLE TONY (1) to place.

BAINBRIDGE (5) burned across to the lead last time out and may have just peaked on his run late when reeled in by the in-form horse Smarter Than You who had the perfect run on his bay. He may be able to burn across to the lead again in this race and could be tough to reel in. TIGER BAND WAGON (6) was able to secure a soft run behind the lead last time out and ran on strongly to get into a clear second behind Captain Shuffles. He draws much less favourably this time and may be forced to do some work in the run. FIRE RAISER (2) put in an excellent run last time out when sitting four back on the pegs and running on nicely into fourth behind Leap To Fame. He should secure a good run close to the speed and should be running on well late. DRAGON (1) has an ideal draw in this race and has been racing in good form. He ran a good third last time out behind the classy Fait Awaits and Regazzo Di Tilly. SELECTIONS: BAINBRIDGE (5), TIGER BAND WAGON (6), FIRE RAISER (2), DRAGON (1) SUGGESTED BET: BAINBRIDGE (5) to win.

KICKING HORSE (2) wasn’t beaten far three starts ago behind NONIS GOLD CLASS (1) in a similar race to this one. He is 10m better off this time and given the small margin between them in that race he should be a good chance of turning the tables. NONIS GOLD CLASS (1) usually steps well from the stand start and should get a good run given the favourable handicap. She was able to lead and win three starts ago beating KICKING HORSE (2) and can look to do the same again in this race. SERENA LOVE (7) was her own worst enemy three starts ago when making a break in the concluding stages which cost her what appeared to be certain victory. She was able to make amends two back winning before running well again last start. BUSTER DAN (6) has been in excellent form recently and was able to score another good win last time out when running over the top late to beat Lochinvar Son. The way the handicaps are in this race he is likely to find this a lot tougher. SELECTIONS: KICKING HORSE (2),NONIS GOLD CLASS (1), SERENA LOVE (7), BUSTER DAN (6) SUGGESTED BET: KICKING HORSE (2) to win.

BARRACUDA (6) scored a good win last time out at Marburg when being forced to race without cover and was just able to prove too strong late. He finds a suitable race where he should be able to work forward and if he can find the front he should take plenty of running down. SWEET ROCKY (9) led last time out and appeared to have his chance there when beaten by Amami. He has now run second in all three of his QLD starts and looks like he has found another race where he can figure in the placings again. PUNTERS JEWEL (4) has excellent gate speed but has seemingly been best in his races when driven with a sit. He got back in the run last time out at Redcliffe over the 2040 and was running on late into eighth. With the right run he could figure in the finish. MARTIN MAGIC (7) was running on strongly last time out into third behind Amami in what was a much better effort. He draws poorly again in this race as a result of his ODM tag and he can look to be running on late again. SELECTIONS: BARRACUDA (6), SWEET ROCKY (9), PUNTERS JEWEL (4), MARTIN MAGIC (7) SUGGESTED BET: BARRACUDA (6) to win.

UBETONRED (7) looked to be terribly unlucky last time out when attempting to get forward early before being forced to the rear of the field and was still just narrowly beaten late in third by Shez A Punter. He should be able to get forward this time and should be hard to beat. HARRY KANE (3) may be able to work across to the lead which should see him hard to beat in a race of this nature. He led three starts ago and was run down late over the 2138 by Smirks Lika Boss. He is likely to have derived benefit from recent runs and should be better suited leading over the 1660. OCTOBER RACKETEER (2) should have the speed to lead initially before having options from there. He was a good winner recently at Marburg when securing a good run off the speed and finishing best to score. MIGHTY IDEAL (8) should get a good run through behind the speed in this race. Secured a good run behind the speed two starts ago at this track and trip and was able finish best to score. He should secure a similar run in this race and can be running on late. SELECTIONS: UBETONRED (7),HARRY KANE (3), OCTOBER RACKETEER (2), MIGHTY IDEAL (8) SUGGESTED BET: UBETONRED(7) to win.

POCKET BOOK (11) hasn’t had much luck in recent outings including last time out when shuffled a long way back. She is likely to be shuffled back again from the outside back row draw but should be suited in this grade of race and can be running on strongly late. ROCKY LEIGH (6) has been trialling up well since joining the stable of Jack Chapple and ran a good third in a recent trial behind Magic Miki. He draws wide and may be forced to do some work in this race but should be hard to beat. TAKE A CHANCE (10) was able to lead recently and was only just run down late by Powermove. He could be put into the race at some stage and can run well again in this company. JIMMY BLING (8) wasn’t beaten far last time out behind Azor Ahai over the 1660 at this track. He will be relying on some luck from inside the back row but looks to find a suitable race. SELECTIONS: POCKET BOOK (11), ROCKY LEIGH (6), TAKE A CHANCE (10), JIMMY BLING (8) SUGGESTED BET: POCKET BOOK (11) to win.

BETTOR BE BOHDI (9) has been a professional place getter since his latest win in late May having placed nine times in twelve starts. He should get a good run in this race and can be hard to beat in this type of company. BETTOR CHEER (4) scored a dominant win recently at this track and trip beating stablemate Next To Me. He was less suited drawing poorly last time out in a strong race taken out by Flying Colours. RACANA (2) secured a good run last time out behind the leader but couldn’t finish it off in a very genuinely run race which was taken out by Cosmic Flyer. She may be able to press to the lead in this race and should be thereabouts. NEXT TO ME (11) was forced to race without cover last time out at Albion Park when finishing fifth in a race the leader King Bobbie bowled along a genuine tempo. He draws poorly in this race and will need a few things to go his way. SELECTIONS: BETTOR BE BOHDI (9), BETTOR CHEER (4), RACANA (2), NEXT TO ME (11) SUGGESTED BET: BETTOR BE BOHDI (9) to win. OVERVIEW:AUSSIE JAY MAC (1) broke stride at the 300m mark and lost approximately 15m before finishing off quickly when an unlucky third (7m) behind My Mate Ace at Shepparton last outing. He has performed well at the trials since and he will take beating if he gives a fool proof display. WICKED HANGOVER (6) is resuming since a Mildura victory in June but he was runner up at a recent Horsham trial effort and should be competitive against this line up. HUNGRY HOGARTH (7) will appreciate a significant drop back in class for this assignment and should go well. He performed a little below expectations when sixth at Charlton last outing but he has been freshened since and his form prior was sound. HALF PRICE BRIDE (2) is drawn to receive an economical trip and is a minor place possibility. BACK: AUSSIE JAY MAC (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: AUSSIE JAY MAC (1), WICKED HANGOVER (6), HUNGRY HOGARTH (7), HALF PRICE BRIDE (2)

OVERVIEW:FEEL THE REIGN (3) settled in eighth position, trailed into the race out three horses wide and hit the line strongly for third behind Altius in a mile rate of 1.56.2 at Kilmore last outing. He produced a strong finish to win at Melton prior and he looms as one of the leading chances again. SPORTING RAGE (2) is a fast beginner and performs best over the sprint distance so he has the conditions to suit him here. He won from behind the leader at Charlton on August 17. SPRINGFIELD RIVER (1) is resuming since a seventh at Cranbourne in June. He will be fitter after two recent trial performances, the latest being a second at Bacchus Marsh and he should receive a nice trip from the pole position. THIS TIME (4) is a former New South Wales pacer, which performed well for a close second at a recent Maryborough trial effort. She made her local debut when she tired late and was unplaced at Maryborough on Monday but she could improve under these conditions. SELECTIONS: FEEL THE REIGN (3), SPORTING RAGE (2), SPRINGFIELD RIVER (1), THIS TIME (4)

OVERVIEW: LATHER ME UP (1) settled on the markers and failed to run on in a heat of the Breeders Challenge at Menangle last week. She was placed in the Group 1 Bathurst Gold Tiara back in March and she is ideally drawn so she appears to be very well placed against this line up. QUEENS BOULEVARD (4) began quickly and worked forward to find the lead when a strong second behind Keayang Hustler at Horsham. She led throughout at a Stawell victory on September 14 and should give another forward showing from her good draw. TOORAM DANNY (6) settled midfield and came out three horses wide from the 600m when a close second at his first run since June. He should strip fitter from that performance and is capable of going one better. YOU’VE BEEN SERVED (5) won easily at Mildura four starts ago and has taken on strong opposition at her past three attempts, the latest being at Globe Derby where she settled down last, tried to sustain a long run and got into third before peaking late. She appears to be better placed under these conditions and is worth thought. OUR PINUP GIRL (7) produced a big performance to score in a mile rate of 1.55.7 at Ballarat then finished unplaced in a strong race at Melton. She is poorly drawn but should be finishing off well. BACK: LATHER ME UP (1) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: LATHER ME UP (1), QUEENS BOULEVARD (4),TOORAM DANNY (6), YOU’VE BEEN SERVED (5)

OVERVIEW: BENNIE AND THE JETS (9) hasn’t raced since July and hasn’t been to the trials but he is clearly the class runner of the field. He won the Elmore and Cobram Cups when he was last in work and was also placed in the Bendigo and Gunbower Cups. OFF YOUR FACESKI (8) produced a strong performance to win under the standing start conditions at Terang last outing. He is a versatile trotter and should give another bold showing. QUEEN KIZEN (5) boasts a consistent standing start record and finished a close second behind Scar at Geelong two starts ago. She performs best when she gains cover close to the pace so commencing from the handicap of 20m is a disadvantage but she is racing too well to dismiss. KENNYWOULD (4) is returning from New South Wales and will be fitter after three placed efforts at the trials. He was a runaway winner at Menangle two starts ago so he cannot be underestimated. SELECTIONS: BENNIE AND THE JETS (9), OFF YOUR FACESKI (8), QUEEN KIZEN (5), KENNYWOULD (4)

OVERVIEW:MILEY KAY (2) finished off nicely when third behind Kings Gallery on debut then had little luck when taking on a strong field in a heat of the Super Series. This is a much easier assignment and she is sure to attract plenty of support. MEGALODON (1) followed the markers throughout when placed at his first two race track appearances then attempted to make ground out wide on the track from the 500m at his latest fifth. He is perfectly drawn to suit his racing pattern and should be competitive under these conditions. CAZADERO (7) was safely held on debut but he settled in a rearward position and the winner Indulgeme recorded a slick mile rate of 1.55.4. He should find this race to be easier and he is a possible improver. SLOWBURN (6) is a New South Wales pacer, which boasts early speed and has claims. The debutante FEARLESS SNIPER (4) has been switched to trainer Boris Devcic after being safely held in four trial performances. He is well drawn first up and must be kept safe. BACK: MILEY KAY (2) – 1 unit (each way) SELECTIONS: MILEY KAY (2), MEGALODON (1), CAZADERO (7), SLOWBURN (6)

OVERVIEW:MAJOR LINCOLN (6) settled in a rearward position and picked up ground without threatening the winner at his latest third. He produced a strong finish to down ESPERANZA (2) at Stawell on September 14 and must be considered as one of the leading chances again. ESPERANZA (2) trailed the leader and used the sprint lane when she appeared to have every chance at her latest second behind MAJOR LINCOLN (6). She scored at Kilmore three starts ago and this race is no harder so she is worth thought again. TALKNPLAY (4) is resuming since a fourth at Bendigo in December but he ran a close second behind the handy type Aussie Jay Mac at a recent Shepparton trial effort. He strikes a suitable field first up and is not without a chance. IVE AN IDEA (5) produced a strong finishing burst when an eye-catching second last outing and cannot be left out of calculations. MASON DIXON LINE (8) finished sixth at Mildura when he was resuming but he was giving the leaders a big start and was making ground late. He should strip fitter from that run and rates as a value hope. SELECTIONS: MAJOR LINCOLN (6), ESPERANZA (2), TALKNPLAY (4), IVE AN IDEA (5)

OVERVIEW: JUSTALITTLESIP (8) has been racing against the Metropolitan open class and will appreciate competing in his easiest assignment for a long time. He was runner up behind He’s From Heaven in a swift mile rate of 1.52.2 five starts ago, which is a strong form pointer for this event. CALEXICO (9) will also appreciate a drop back in class from his recent efforts and battled on well after enduring a tough run at his latest fifth behind Fairplay. He is a strong 4yo pacer and should make his presence felt. LOUGLE (4) has been racing very well but without luck and warrants respect. He is versatile and is better drawn than his recent performances. MAXY WANTS TO PLAY (2) and EARL OF PEMBROKE (3) are both racing well enough to feature prominently in a quality field. BACK: JUSTALITTLESIP (8) – 1.5 units (each way) SELECTIONS: JUSTALITTLESIP (8), CALEXICO (9), LOUGLE (4), EARL OF PEMBROKE (3)

OVERVIEW: KING SAINT (6) chased hard when a close second behind the smart pacer Ultimate Vinnie last outing. He battled on well for a close second behind Dembe (won again since) prior and he is capable of going one better here. TO THE NINES (8) ran a game race when making late ground in fast time at Melton then had no luck whatsoever after being headed off at the start at his latest Mildura third. He couldn’t have drawn worse but he is racing in career best form and deserves to break through for a win. NEW YORKER (9) was left stranded on the outside of the leader throughout and fought on well when fourth behind Mount Barker Boy at Melton last outing. He has been racing well at Metropolitan level and should be competitive under these conditions. OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (7) didn’t have much luck at Melton last outing and is capable of showing improvement. SELECTIONS: KING SAINT (6), TO THE NINES (8), NEW YORKER (9), OUR VINCENT CAN GOGH (7)

OVERVIEW: KNOW THE SCORE (1) has been racing consistently well without winning recently. He finished second last start at Ballarat, flashing home after navigating wide from three back on the fence. He has the ace barrier here and should have enough gate speed to hold a forward position. OZZIE DIAMOND (10) has been in flying form, winning her last two starts at this track. She has a brilliant turn of foot but will need to overcome barrier 10 over the short trip. STERLING GIGI (7) has equal-best sectional times with Ozzie Diamond in this field. He has consistently been running solid races without winning, but the race map is his biggest obstacle here. GLENLINE (2) is a brilliant swooper who won well last start. Barrier two should allow him to settle in a striking position and threaten late again. Also respecting KEAYANG ALABAMA (9), who is first-up since March. BACK: KNOW THE SCORE (1) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: KNOW THE SCORE (1), OZZIE DIAMOND (10), STERLING GIGI (7), GLENLINE (2)

OVERVIEW: LITTLE MISS VALLEY (9) finished ninth last start, but that was in the Group 1 Vicbred Super Series Final for four-year-old mares behind Gatesys Gem and I Am Wilma. Her previous run was a fourth in the heat, where she hit the line strongly from well back. She will appreciate the drop in class and looks hard to beat. DISTANT SUN (8) was a good second last start at Geelong. He worked to the breeze and remained strong late. He can make his own luck here. VOLDAGHA (5) had a tough run last start and tired a little late. He is a nice horse who will be a threat if he maps well. WALLIS (7) has a tricky barrier to overcome. If he can find the gaps late, he will be competitive. He has a good relationship with driver James Herbertson, who jumps back on here. BACK: LITTLE MISS VALLEY (9) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:LITTLE MISS VALLEY (9), DISTANT SUN (8), VOLDAGHA (5), WALLIS (7)

OVERVIEW: HURRICANE HOOLY (10) looked strong when letting down late for third at Ballarat. She has a great turn of foot and, if she gets a good trip into the race, she will be the one to watch late. WHERES WOOD WOOD (8) is in great form, with three seconds and a win in her recent record. She has a great turn of foot but can also race tough, as shown by her second at Shepparton last start. Barrier eight is tricky, as she may get shuffled back early. IMAGUNNARESTNGO (1) should get a comfortable trip along the fence from barrier one and could be in the finish late. GOZO MAJOR (5) was huge when winning two starts ago, racing three wide for most of the event. He can make his own luck and has the best sectional times in this field. Also noting the interesting FINANCIAL BURDEN (3), who hasn’t raced for more than 600 days and was last campaigning in Queensland. SELECTIONS:HURRICANE HOOLY (10), WHERES WOOD WOOD (8), IMAGUNNARESTNGO (1), GOZO MAJOR (5)

OVERVIEW: This is a competitive event with plenty of chances, making it difficult to narrow the selections down to four runners. STRAIGHT TO THETOP (5) rarely runs a bad race and has the gate speed to map positively. She ran a solid second behind the talented Little Miss Morgan last start. ABBIE (6) is having her fourth start this campaign and is improving with each run as she gets closer to her best form. She raced tough in the breeze last start and was strong to the line. Expecting a good showing here, although the barrier makes things tricky. CONSTANT (10) is a great swooper with the best sectional times in this event. She will be flying home late. Expecting a good showing from MAJESTIC MONARCH (4) if he can map well. SELECTIONS:STRAIGHT TO THETOP (5), ABBIE (6), CONSTANT (10), MAJESTIC MONARCH (4)

OVERVIEW: KEAYANG MINNESOTA (11) is a very talented trotter, but her manners have been an issue throughout her career. If she trots throughout, she should be winning. Barrier 11 gives her time and space to settle early. ALDEBARAN MARCUS (7) ran a tough third last start, racing in the breeze and still hitting the line well. Barrier seven is tricky, but he can make his own luck. KALARNEY PRINCE (4) is the emergency who has gained a start following an early scratching. He was an impressive winner last start, settling three back on the fence before dashing home once clear to win by more than 12 metres. MOONSHINE LOUIE (3) can perform well with the right run and looks likely to map favourably from barrier three. SELECTIONS:KEAYANG MINNESOTA (11), ALDEBARAN MARCUS (7), KALARNEY PRINCE (4), MOONSHINE LOUIE (3)

OVERVIEW:SMARTY BART (9) looks a very exciting first starter for Craig and Abbey Turnbull. He ran 1:56.5 in a recent Cobram trial. Barrier nine suits, as it allows him to settle early, which is ideal for a horse with limited experience. KEAYANG MARICRUZ (5) has had two career starts. She was good on debut when finishing second but underperformed at her second start, with stewards noting she was “unable to quicken with them when the tempo increased in the concluding stages”. She has had a month between runs to freshen up and can bounce back here. GOODMORNING MIKI (6) is a well-bred filly who is yet to get it right with her manners. Her race performances haven’t been a true indication of her ability, and her trials have been more encouraging. If she gets it right here, we could see the best of her. HEAVENLY NIKKY (8) continues to surprise me as a maiden. She rarely puts in a bad run but often finds a few rivals a little too good. She should be competitive again here. BACK: SMARTY BART (9) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: SMARTY BART (9), KEAYANG MARICRUZ (5), GOODMORNING MIKI (6), HEAVENLY NIKKY (8)

OVERVIEW: MY MATE ACE (8) is a talented horse in great form. He has had two starts this year, and although things haven’t gone his way on either occasion, he has still managed to win impressively. He looks progressive and can win again here. OUR ULTIMATE LOIS (3) is first-up in the state for Paul Tonkin. She moves into barrier two following a scratching and may appreciate the change of scenery. TRYX VIXEN (1) is a smart mare at her best. She recently competed in the Vicbred Super Series against the best mares in the state. She can make her own luck but should enjoy a good trip from barrier one here. LOU WILL (7) is a nice horse at his best but has been performing slightly below his best recently. He drops in class here, although the tricky barrier remains a concern. BACK: MY MATE ACE (8) – 3 units (win) SELECTIONS:MY MATE ACE (8), OUR ULTIMATE LOIS (3), TRYX VIXEN (1), LOU WILL (7)

OVERVIEW: OVER HERE (7) was a deserving favourite last start but got it wrong with his manners. Despite that, his performance was outstanding. He galloped early, tailed out, then caught the field and still hit the line well. If he trots throughout here, he will be hard to beat. KYVALLEY JOYRIDE (1) gets the ace barrier and should enjoy a comfortable trip. With the right run, he can capitalise. FIRST IN FLIGHT (6) is a first starter for Jason Hackett. She finished second in a recent Bacchus Marsh trial, although it was run in slow time. We will learn more about her here. SYNTAX ERROR (4) doesn’t have the strongest numerical form but has the best sectional times on exposed form in this field. With the right run, she could turn her form around. Also respecting DANCE WITH ROXY (3) after a confidence-boosting second last start. SELECTIONS: OVER HERE (7), KYVALLEY JOYRIDE (1), FIRST IN FLIGHT (6), SYNTAX ERROR (4)

OVERVIEW: MAAS BETTING AGAIN (3) is a high-speed mare for Alison and Chris Alford. She should be able to find the front with her great gate speed and will be hard to beat over the short trip. TOORAM MAGIC (6) is a talented gelding resuming here after more than 130 days away from racing. Two starts ago, he finished second behind the talented Major Blitz at Bendigo. Fitness is a query, particularly from the awkward barrier. DEMBE (2) is a talented son of Lochinvar Art who is in great form. He has proven his versatility, winning both from the front and with a sit, as well as when racing tough. This is another step up in class. HELLOVATIME (1) is an ultra-consistent horse who is racing very well. He should get a good trip along the fence here. SELECTIONS:MAAS BETTING AGAIN (3), TOORAM MAGIC (6), DEMBE (2), HELLOVATIME (1) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

SONARMI JOH (9) has a terrific record here at Mount Gambier where he has won five from eleven starts. He will need some luck off the handicap but he does look the one to beat tonight. ITGETSBETTER (1) rarely wins but he finds an easier race tonight and he has to be taken seriously off the front mark. JAKEE BOY (3) and CAITHNESS LADY (4) are also chances.

EASTBRO KAZ (6) does her best racing here at Mount Gambier where she has had six starts for two wins and three placings. She will need some luck from the draw but she looks like the one to beat in an even race. WE FAVOUR ROSIE (1) is another who races well here at Mount Gambier. She is a strong chance from the inside draw. OUR BELLA LUCIA (5) and PRESIDENTIALCHANGE (7) are also chances.

SMOKIN STREPO (7) was a last start winner here at Mount Gambier in June. The second row draw isn’t ideal but if he can lob into a nice position then he should be attacking the line if he is fully fit. DANCIN WITH ELVIS (1) is a chance of finding the lead and running a very strong race out in front. BAYSIDE VICTORY (2) and THE IRISHMAN (3) are also chances.

WICKED THREE (7) has had the one start for one win at Globe Derby where he defeated SIENNA BELLA by 3.6 meters. A repeat of that run will make him hard to beat again. MALINI JOH (4), AMERICAN SQUARED (3) and SHOWNOFEAR (2) are also chances.

SPOOK CROCKER (4) won the Mount Gambier gold cup earlier in the year and was the most dominant horse in Mount Gambier before going for a spell. He has in form driver Hannah Lewis in the sulky who is fresh off winning The Radiant at Port Pirie on Saturday night. It’s hard to see him losing despite being first up. YANKEE MOJOH (1) is the main danger. She will love the inside draw and she has won two out of her last three at Ballarat and Melton. BUBBA SCRUB (6) and GRINNING BEACH BOY (2) are also chances.

THE BLAZINGBOOTS (2) has been racing well without winning in Victoria recently. Tonight is an easier race for him. If he can get the right run then he should be hard to beat. EASTBRO MIKA (6), LUCKY VINCENT (5) and FRANKIE UNDER FIRE (4) are also chances. OVERVIEW:MAJOR ORION (5) has been good in his runs for the Douglas stable, performing well from tricky draws and set-ups. He attempted to lead here last week unsuccessfully and sat parked thereafter in quick time for this grade. The map looks more favourable to cross to the pegs this time and find the top, and from there he’ll take plenty of catching. ELIZAJANE (7) has been racing well this season and, despite the wide draw, is likely to press forward over the short trip. Whether she has the speed to lead is questionable, but even if she sits parked, she is well placed and can hang tough. WICKED MITZI (8) isn’t in great numerical form but gets a soft run from the back row here, and with Herbertson booked becomes a blowout hope if the breaks come. INTERPRETATION (9) drops in grade, and the Dembe form he’s been exposed to over his past couple of runs looks to be decent form. He was forced to sit parked last week and may be better coming with one run if the pace is right. BACK: MAJOR ORION (5) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:MAJOR ORION (5), ELIZAJANE (7), WICKED MITZI (8), INTERPRETATION (9)

OVERVIEW: A standing start for the trotters here over the middle distance, which often makes it difficult for the backmarkers. However, the front-row brigade isn’t going all that well. STRAIGHT TO THETOP (7) loves the standing-start conditions and was a winner at this track and distance, from the same handicap, back in August against a similar line-up. She turned in a good run last week behind a smart one, and with the right run in transit can be strong late. KENNYS SON (9) is off a 30m handicap, but in his favour are sound standing-start manners and a win at this track. He was a winner here under mobile conditions two back, but the concern is that he broke in running either side of that. WATCH AND ACT (8) is the most reliable under these conditions, with 10 of his 14 wins coming from the tapes. He hasn’t won in 20 tries this season, however, but his manners will carry him a long way. KYVALLEY MISTY (3) gets the front-row advantage and has been okay from the stand in the past, but her run last start at Melton was not up to scratch. She was a winner in an easier race three back and gets Alford, so she’s worth keeping safe if you can overlook her last start. MASSIF CENTRAL (4) has only had the one standing start and, although beaten a long way, was quick away from the tapes. He’s a horse who likes to lead, but normally over the mile. He’s winless from 33 attempts at this distance but has place claims. BACK: STRAIGHT TO THETOP (7) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS:STRAIGHT TO THETOP (7), KENNYS SON (9), WATCH AND ACT (8), KYVALLEY MISTY (3)

OVERVIEW: Tricky affair with little exposed form to draw upon with confidence. MYSTIC MOVER (7) is the exception to that observation, having placed in 3 of 5 starts, including a good 2nd last start at Kilmore behind an in-form winner. The gate is no spoil, but over the short trip and against an apparent lack of opposition, she may be obliged to press forward and give herself every chance. SON OF A BROAD (11) did plenty of work first up, but that’s normally the way he races and, to be fair, a bit more was expected. He does have a very in-form stable and driver, so be prepared to forgive last time and expect him to put his best foot forward here. Then there are a few runners who are a market watch and require a bit of guesswork. HOLLOW LOG (6) is an emergency and, interestingly, a well-bred 7yo first starter. He’s only had the one trial and showed great gate speed to finish 3rd, which was okay. He should be considered if he gets a run and is a market watch. ITS JUST RUBY (5) joins the Paul Tonkin stable, which often improves this type of horse fresh, so although the form isn’t there and she’s first up without a trial, she must be kept safe. The two stablemates, TAMALIA (2), who galloped away on debut, and EVA EXPRESS (3), haven’t done too much at the trials, but in fairness they were against better-rated types, and this stable is worth respecting. SELECTIONS:MYSTIC MOVER (7), SON OF A BROAD (11), HOLLOW LOG (6), ITS JUST RUBY (5)

OVERVIEW:MAJOR DRAMA (7) has been turning in some decent runs for the new stable, and she hasn’t had the best set-ups to put her best on display. She gets no favours with the draw, but this looks to be her most winnable race, dropping in class and looking well placed with the claim of in-form junior driver Blake Pace. She will need luck in running, but her second-last run was good enough to expect improvement. MADAM REACTOR (6) gets back to a more suitable grade, with some acceptable performances against tougher company. The map may be a bit sticky, but she looks well graded. PIRANI PERFECT (2) is a 3yo filly having her first run for the Rebecca Bartley stable, which deserves respect at its home track. She was a trial winner here recently and, from the positive draw, can race in a nice position. Her race form isn’t great, but any market push warrants attention. ROCK POSTER (4) is an honest mare who’s enjoying a solid season. She’s second up from a break and was good last time out when 3rd in the same race as the top pick. A positive draw helps her chances. It’s hard to know what to make of MIKIS PLEASURE (8) on current form, but she has won 3 from 12 starts, albeit with her best form coming a couple of years back. She’s had plenty of trials and is worth keeping safe for multiples. SELECTIONS:MAJOR DRAMA (7), MADAM REACTOR (6), PIRANI PERFECT (2), ROCK POSTER (4)

OVERVIEW:IMAWINGATE (5) is back to the grade he races best in, and his last victory in July came in similar grade with Herbertson aboard. He can slide forward alongside the likely leader and potentially find a good map. He’s a 10-time winner from 33 tries here, which is a much stronger record than many of these can boast. TREACHEROUSTIMES (4) looks the likely leader in the race and does race best from that position. He’s limited with the times he’s capable of, so if he gets control of the race, he will take some catching. BLUE CANNON (3) is an interesting runner, given that he’s been rough in his action this campaign, which is surprising for a horse of his experience. His best form has him well in this, so he’s worth keeping safe if he does everything right. Worth noting at the minor end are KRAKEY (6), ZEUSS (7) and MISTER RAUDONIKIS (8), who have drawn awkwardly and have been going fairly but would need to improve significantly to win. BACK: IMAWINGATE (5) – 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: IMAWINGATE (5), TREACHEROUSTIMES (4), BLUE CANNON (3), KRAKEY (6)

OVERVIEW:MELICAN (8) looks to be a 2yo filly going places, unbeaten in two race starts, the most recent of which saw her bolt in when able to lead. She goes to the back row now, but without a horse drawn outside her, she can map in a striking position. This is a tougher race and set-up, but hopefully that means a better price to play, as she looks the one to beat again. CRACKIN PHILTRA (5) is fresh up from a break off a couple of good trials and was good last preparation, winning before the spell in decent time. The trainer/driver combination deserves respect and should get the right map to have every chance. OZZIE TART (3) finished in the quinella behind the top pick last time but was beaten a long way. She has very good gate speed to get a good map and be a chance again. MAJOR FRIEND (6) was a good winner here last week in an easier race from a back-row draw. That performance keeps her in the mix, but this is a step up. THE KING OFTHEROAD (7) is first up and was racing well before a break. This draw and the quality of opposition mean a bit needs to go his way, so place claims look best. BACK: MELICAN (8) – 3.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: MELICAN (8), CRACKIN PHILTRA (5), OZZIE TART (3), MAJOR FRIEND (6)

OVERVIEW:YELLA (6) drops in grade for this and was good last week from a bad draw, where he drifted back to last and made good ground late. He can show speed, but it’s hard to know how the map plays out here. He’s going well enough to win again but will need luck in running. SHEZABLUECHIP (4) has a good strike rate at this track, with 50% of her wins coming here. She can show gate speed from this draw and be driven assertively to look for the front. She was a winner when on the peg line two back. ICANMOTOR (3) has been getting some ace steers from Jordy Leedham, but he just can’t seem to crack it for a win, although he has still been consistent. He can look to cross to the pegs and have options from there. JOEYS HANGOVER (5) didn’t have much luck here last week when dropping back to last after being caught wide. His runs have been sound this time in, and he has claims again. QUEENHIGH FLUSH (7) looks the only other hope for the Quaddie, and while she has ability and can give a good sight, the draw hurts. SELECTIONS: YELLA (6), SHEZABLUECHIP (4), ICANMOTOR (3), JOEYS HANGOVER (5)

OVERVIEW:OZZIE DIAMOND (8) is a 2yo filly giving away experience here, but she’s been good in her career so far, performing well in the Vicbred Series, and was a solid winner last time out at Kilmore, albeit from a better draw when she was able to map well. The claim gets her in well on the ratings scale, and if the tempo is solid enough, she can be strong late. LAVADA GOLD (2) was better last time out at Cranbourne when 2nd from a bad draw, finding the line strongly late along the inside. A better draw now and a repeat of that last run have him well in it. TASTE IT (4) has two wins and four minor placings from 19 starts this season. Glenn Bull gets a workable gate, and the horse has enough demonstrated ability for this type of grade. MISS PIGGY WIGGY (7) has three wins this season and a faster best mile rate, but gate seven makes the map challenging to overcome. Her best form warrants respect at this level, however. SELECTIONS:OZZIE DIAMOND (8), LAVADA GOLD (2), TASTE IT (4), MISS PIGGY WIGGY (7)
